newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish automotive output shrinks in August.
newsitem.headline: Turkish automotive output shrinks in August.

text.p: Turkey's motor vehicle output fell 22 from a year ago to 13,394 in August, due to month-long annual holidays and maintenance in leading car maker Tofas , the association of Turkish automotive industry (OSD) said.
Total output rose 12 percent to 206,926 in January-August this year, compared to the same 1995 period, OSD said in its monthly bulletin.
Only 4,347 cars were produced last month, down 60 percent from a year ago and compared to 22,090 in July. Eigth-month car output was 137,074, versus 135,905 in the same 1995 period.

OSD said 138,750 cars were sold in Turkey in the first eight months of 1996, including 27,839 imported cars, compared to a sale figure of 126,555, including 9,283 imported ones in January-August 1995.
The share of imported cars in the domestic market almost tripled to 20.1 percent over the same period.

Eight-month output jumped 59 percent from the same 1995 period to 16,370 in trucks, 58 percent to 3,125 in midibuses, 43 percent to 31,142 in tractors and 22 percent to 11,827 in pick ups. Bus production more than doubled to 1,617 over the same period.
OSD said Turkey's motor vehicle and automotive parts exports grew by 29 percent to $933.02 million in January-August.

Car exports totalled $227.9 million, up 67 percent from the first eight months of 1995, followed by bus exports worth $132.2 million, up 91 percent and tyre exports of $157.4 million, down four percent. -- Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875.
